articles.title: You All Guessed Elder Scrolls 6’s Name, And Now Here’s The Game’s Setup – Report
articles.summary: After eight years, Xbox is reportedly preparing to reintroduce The Elder Scrolls VI to the world. And this time, the game will apparently get an official subtitle: Sentinel. According to The Verge, Bethesda could reveal the full name next month in celebration of Skyrim's 15th anniversary.
body: The report states that Hammerfell will serve as the setting for Sentinel. It's a massive region that's southwest of Skyrim and probably best known for being playable in The Elder Scrolls Online. As for the narrative, the RPG "will be the first game about the history of the Elder Scrolls," per The Verge. That means discovering "the secrets of these mysterious ancient artifacts" in Sentinel.

It's unknown how much Bethesda will showcase, if the re-reveal does in fact happen in November. However, the report states that gameplay demonstrations are taking place, following up Xbox CEO Asha Sharma saying she saw the game in August. At that time, Sharma teased The Elder Scrolls VI's subtitle, and fans correctly figured out it's Sentinel --at least reportedly right now. She also noted that the game's "scale and grandeur are incredible."

Earlier this year, Skyrim director Todd Howard expressed that he knows his team at Bethesda needs "to get it right" with The Elder Scrolls VI. The majority of people at Bethesda Game Studios are working on the RPG currently.
points: After eight years, Xbox is reportedly preparing to reintroduce The Elder Scrolls VI to the world.
And this time, the game will apparently get an official subtitle: Sentinel.
According to The Verge, Bethesda could reveal the full name next month in celebration of Skyrim's 15th anniversary.
The report states that Hammerfell will serve as the setting for Sentinel.

articles.title: Save $200 Off the 27" Samsung Odyssey OLED G6 240Hz Gaming Monitor Ahead of Black Friday
articles.summary: Ahead of Black Friday, Amazon is offering a great deal on a well-rated OLED gaming monitor. You can pick up a 27" Samsung Odyssey OLED G6 QHD 240Hz gaming monitor, which normally retails for $600, for just $399.99 with free delivery after a $200 off instant discount.
body: The Samsung Odyssey OLED G6 is a current generation (2026) 27" QD-OLED monitor with 2560x1440 resolution, which equates to a pixel density of 109ppi. It's sharp enough for both gaming and general workstation use with excellent text clarity. This monitor is equipped with Samsung's quantum dot (QD) OLED panel. A QD OLED panel is brighter and has a wider color gamut than the more common W-OLED panel. OLED monitors in general offer superior image quality compared to other monitors thanks to a near-instantaneous response time, true black levels, and near-infinite contrast ratio.

Most "budget" OLED monitors have a native 120Hz-165Hz refresh rate, but the Samsung Odyssey OLED G6 boasts a native 240Hz refresh rate. This makes it an excellent option for first person shooters, sports games, or any other game that involves high-speed motion or requires twitch-like reflexes. You'll need to make sure you have an appropriate graphics card to achieve 240fps at 1440p, ideally something like an RTX 5070 Ti or AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT, although an RTX 5070 should be able to hit this target in older games like Fortnite, Apex Legends, Counter-Strike, or Valorant.
points: Ahead of Black Friday, Amazon is offering a great deal on a well-rated OLED gaming monitor.

articles.title: The Elder Scrolls 6 Is Reportedly Subtitled 'Sentinel,' New Story Details Revealed Ahead of Rumored Announcement
articles.summary: A new report claims the next Elder Scrolls game will be titled The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel, along with new story details. According to The Verge, The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel is the title of the highly-anticipated follow-up to Bethesda's Skyrim.
body: All of this is pretty exciting and shows that the game is likely getting closer to release. While we're not quite sure when to expect The Elder Scrolls 6, it wouldn't be surprising if we hear more details next year ahead of a 2028 release. However, Bethesda does like to wait until its games are close to the finish line to really lay it all out there, so we may be waiting a while before we get raw gameplay.

The road to The Elder Scrolls 6 has been quite long, as Bethesda announced the game back in 2018. At that stage, the game was still in the very, very early stages of pre-production. It may not have even really been anything more than a concept at that point, since Bethesda was full steam ahead on Starfield, which wouldn't release for another five years from that point. Since shipping Starfield, The Elder Scrolls 6 has become a massive priority and the studio's focus going forward.

Although there is a lot happening in and around Bethesda with future Fallout games, re-releases, and Starfield updates, The Elder Scrolls 6 seems to be taking the bulk of the developer's focus. The only question now is: will it all be worth the long wait?
points: A new report claims the next Elder Scrolls game will be titled The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel, along with new story details.
According to The Verge, The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel is the title of the highly-anticipated follow-up to Bethesda's Skyrim.

articles.title: Xbox Wants To Be More Profitable Than PlayStation And Nintendo By 2030
articles.summary: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has an ambitious goal: not only to make Xbox more lucrative, but to surpass the profit margins of its biggest gaming rivals, Sony and Nintendo. Speaking to CNBC, Sharma said Microsoft was working to achieve this goal by mid-2030 and had a variety of plans in place, from…
body: "By Financial Year 2030, our ambition is to be halfway to our long-term daily-player goal with sustained double-digit growth in players and engagement and industry-leading margins," she wrote.

While Sharma aims to increase Xbox's player and revenue growth in the fiscal year ending June 2027, things don't look too good for the division right now. According to Circana tracking data, US Xbox Series hardware sales fell 27% year-over-year in September 2026--reaching a new all-time September low--and Sharma recently posted online that revenue had declined in the most recent financial quarter. Sharma added that "console sales remain constrained by supply," but she was vague on the specifics. At the same time, Xbox console prices rose again in August, making it more expensive than ever to buy one compared with its original launch price in November 2020.

articles.title: The Ultra-Slim Baseus Blade 20,000mAh Power Bank Drops to $39 Ahead of Black Friday
articles.summary: Looking for a high-capacity, high-output power bank with an ultra-slim footprint? Ahead of Black Friday, Amazon has dropped the price of the Baseus Blade 20,000mAh 100W power bank to just $39.49 shipped after you apply coupon code " Z6J1ANOV ". You do NOT have to be an Amazon Prime member.
body: The Baseus Blade measures only 0.7 inches thick. Most high-capacity power banks are well over 1" in thickness. The Blade achieves this slim depth by going with a wider body design. The form factor allows it to fit perfectly in a laptop bag or backpack sleeve. It still weighs in at about one pound which is comparable to other power banks, so no give or take there.

The wide body allows it to squeeze in four ports: two USB Type-C ports each with 100W of Power Delivery and two USB Type-A ports each with 30W output. Note that the maximum charging output is 100W. That means although all three ports add up to a total of 160W, only a maximum of 100W will be delivered across all three ports if they are used simultaneously.

The Baseus Blade has USB Type-C ports that provides up to 100W of power output but it will automatically throttle down to whatever maximum rate the plugged-in device accepts. The Nintendo Switch and Switch 2 can only accept a maximum of 18W-30W of power output. The Steam Deck can accept up to 45W. The Legion Go S accepts up to 55W. The Xbox ROG Ally X can actually accept charging rates of up to 100W.
points: Looking for a high-capacity, high-output power bank with an ultra-slim footprint?
Ahead of Black Friday, Amazon has dropped the price of the Baseus Blade 20,000mAh 100W power bank to just $39.49 shipped after you apply coupon code " Z6J1ANOV ".

articles.title: RAMageddon Will Only Get Worse in 2027, According to Samsung
articles.summary: The entirety of 2026 has been defined by an ongoing RAM crisis, causing price increases on everything from the PS5 to the Steam Machine. And, according to Samsung's latest earnings report, it's only going to get worse over the next year.
body: In its Q3 2026 earnings call, it was shared that Samsung's semiconductor segment, which includes its memory business, made the company 147.1 trillion Korean Won, of which 106.5 trillion is profit. That makes up for 72% of all of Samsung's revenue in the last quarter. And according to Samsung, those numbers were possible by prioritizing the manufacturing of the HBM4 memory used in AI datacenters.

Looking forward, Samsung expects the memory market to tighten even more in 2027, with the company claiming "Surging AI-driven demand likely to further tighten supply shortages compared with CY26," when talking about the memory business next year. AI demand is so strong that Samsung doesn't even mention consumer-grade DDR5 memory, and is instead focused entirely on building a "stable sales base through long-term contracts and ensure timely readiness of new products tailored to requirements for AI applications."
points: The entirety of 2026 has been defined by an ongoing RAM crisis, causing price increases on everything from the PS5 to the Steam Machine.
And, according to Samsung's latest earnings report, it's only going to get worse over the next year.

articles.title: Xbox’s Recent Efforts Haven’t Changed Anything And The Future Remains Bleak, Expert Says
articles.summary: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has undertaken a number of efforts thus far to help get the business back into a healthy place, and nothing has worked, Circana analyst Mat Piscatella says.
body: He told The Game Business that based on the sales and engagement data he sees for the US gaming industry, "I'm not seeing [the moves] have any positive impact" for Xbox.

The disc-to-digital program "hasn't changed their sales of new physical software trend at all," he added. Additionally, making Gears of War: E-Day exclusive on console to Xbox "hasn't made any difference" in terms of selling more Xbox hardware. In fact, Xbox sales continue to spiral. Sharma says there is a supply issue, but, in the US at least, you can get a new Xbox very easily.

Piscatella said E-Day is a "Gears-ass Gears of War game," and a gorgeous one. But making it exclusive to Xbox created a scenario where "you chop the legs out" from under its potential potential to boost Xbox generally. "At least in the short term, it hasn't made a difference," he said.

There was clear and obvious evidence that E-Day was planned for PS5, but it was never released on Sony's console. Other industry experts said Microsoft purposefully sent E-Day out to die "for hearts and minds."

articles.title: Phantom Blade Zero Is Already Proving Its Prelaunch Hype Was No Fluke
articles.summary: Just a few hours into launch, Phantom Blade Zero is already a hit game on PC. There was considerable hype behind the game as it was estimated that it had sold 1 million units before launch, and at the time of writing, it has peaked on Steam with 723,876 concurrent players.
body: Alinea Analytics' Rhys Elliott gave a breakdown of those preorder sales--when they had reached 850,000 units sold--explaining that 62.5% of Phantom Blade Zero's pre-launch sales came from China, Taiwan, and Hong Kong. "These markets--but predominantly China--account for 75.9% of the copies on Steam and about 24.9% on PS5," Elliott wrote, noting that the early sales had generated $43 million in revenue.

In a launch-day letter, creative director Soulframe Liang thanked the fans for Phantom Blade Zero's strong start, and the people in his studio, S-Game, for bringing his vision to life. "This is a game of immense scale, made with all the passion in our hearts. It is a gift from a small group of gamers who just happen to be developers, to every gamer who shares our love for gaming," Liang wrote.

articles.title: BioWare Co-Founder Breaks Down the Problem With AI in Game Development Perfectly
articles.summary: When Electronic Arts decided to shutter legendary RPG studio BioWare on Oct. 21, Greg Zeschuk, one of BioWare's co-founders alongside Ray Muzyka and Augustine Yip, found out through a flurry of text messages.
body: "I didn't have the immediate impact,” Zeschuk told 80 Level, speaking from his home in Edmonton — the home of BioWare. "I wasn't there to share in the moment, which in some ways was nice because I was able to kind of just take my time with it."

Zeschuk clarified that this didn't mean the closure wasn't sad or monumental, adding that Edmonton would be hit the hardest by the studio's shutdown. However, Zeschuk said he and his fellow co-founder, Muzyka, had already said their emotional goodbye when they left the studio in 2012. His empathy, however, is more reserved for those who have lost their jobs.
"Anyone getting put into the job hunt is a sort of terrifying endeavor and super sad,” Zeschuk said.

While Zeschuk's feelings about BioWare's closure weren't overtly emotional, he had plenty of passion and ire to direct at executives with no game development experience, and at their over-involvement and reliance on AI.
points: When Electronic Arts decided to shutter legendary RPG studio BioWare on Oct.

articles.title: 28 Years Later, Ocarina of Time’s Saddest Line Is Still the Best in Zelda History
articles.summary: Few things can elicit a good cry like a sad video game. And Roger… ’s gut-punch portrayal of living with dementia. Spiritfarer ’s calming meditation on life, death, and the passage between.
body: Maybe a good cry isn’t always the reason we play games, but it springs upon us nevertheless. And one of the strongest instances actually dates back two decades, to Nintendo’s totemic 3D adventure game The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time.

Early in the adventure, after proving he has what it takes to be a hero and receiving the blessing of the dying Great Deku Tree, young Link finally prepares to say goodbye to Kokiri Forest. Before he can venture past its edge, his childhood friend catches up to him. Saria is sad to see him go, but she has a parting gift for him: the ocarina from which the game gets its name.
“I knew… that you would leave the forest… someday, Link,” she says. “Because you’re different from me and my friends… But that’s OK, because we’ll be friends forever…won’t we?”

articles.title: Dataminer uncovers that Spiny - a character seemingly with no way to operate a car - was meant to be playable in Mario Kart World
articles.summary: A dataminer has uncovered something peculiar in the code of Mario Kart World. Spiny, a tiny little turtle-looking fella with a spiky shell, was meant to be a driver in the game.
body: This information was discovered by Bluesky user Benial, with Spiny's internal name 'Togezo' listed alongside a selection of other characters. As of writing there's been no model, animation, nor idea of how exactly Spiny would imagine such a feat discovered.

Spiny, for those who don't know, is a menacing creature not particularly known for its driving prowess. 'Spiny' has long been the name for the enemies initially introduced in Super Mario Bros., and has been a staple of the Mario universe since 1985. With that angry look on his face and the spikes lining his shell, one would worry whether it's a good idea to let them behind the wheel at all.

Hey, why not? Boo is a playable driver, and the veteran ghost character also doesn't seem like the driving type. So Spiny may have made a great addition to the roster. Why is it my business whether Spiny has trouble driving a car or not; No one elected me to police the Rainbow Roads.

articles.title: Game Pass Just Finally Got One of the Best Horror Games in Years
articles.summary: If you were to try to pick the best horror game of the 2020s so far, you’d have a very long list to choose from. Between multiple Resident Evil games, a successful revival of the Silent Hill franchise, and a slew of landmark indies like Signalis, the horror genre has been in a true renaissance over…
body: Mouthwashing became an instant cult hit when it was released in 2024, sandwiched between heavy hitters like Astro Bot and Silent Hill 2. Steady word of mouth helped it escape a busy season for big games and become Steam’s best-kept secret. Now, it finally makes its way to Nintendo Switch, PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X — just in time for Halloween. It's also available on Xbox Game Pass starting today. If you’ve yet to play it, now’s the perfect chance to try a game that hasn’t left my mind for two years.

Mouthwashing is a narrative-driven horror game set aboard a cargo spaceship. After crashing into an asteroid, the ship’s crew is left stranded in space with dwindling resources. The crew mostly survives the crash, but one member, Curly, is nearly killed. The eeriest recurring image in a game full of them is Curly’s body, fully bandaged like a mummy with only a bloodshot eye poking out.
points: If you were to try to pick the best horror game of the 2020s so far, you’d have a very long list to choose from.

articles.title: 'Celeste' and 'Towerfall' Delisted From Xbox as Dev Joins Boycott
articles.summary: Celeste and Towerfall are no longer on Xbox. Developer Maddy Thorson has explained why in a social media post: to support the ongoing pro-Palestinian Boycott, Divestment, and Sanctions (BDS) movement against Microsoft.
body: Celeste, which happens to be one of the best 2D platformers ever made, was released in 2018 for PC, Switch, PS4, and Xbox One, while Towerfall: Ascension is a single-screen multiplayer action game that Polygon once described as "the new gold standard in the local multiplayer renaissance."

Thorson isn’t the first developer to voice support for BDS's boycott against Microsoft over its ties to the Israeli military. A few weeks ago, Big Walk developer House House said its game would not come to Xbox in support of BDS. “It has always been our intention for Big Walk to be played by groups of friends, and we know that keeping the game off Xbox runs counter to those intentions,” the studio said in a statement. “This decision means that some people will miss out on playing Big Walk with their friends, and we understand the disappointment we’re causing. We are disappointed too.”

articles.title: EA's sale to Saudi-led consortium was "final nail in the coffin" for BioWare, says studio co-founder
articles.summary: One of BioWare's famous doctor-founders, Greg Zeschuk, has finally spoken about the studio's closure last week, saying it's "kind of sad" and that EA's leveraged buyout by a Saudi-involved consortium "was the final nail in the coffin".
body: By the time he flew home later, he'd already apparently digested the news and missed most of the discourse around it. "I wasn't there to share in the moment," he said, "which in some ways was nice because I was able to kind of just take my time with it.

"I'm not saying it doesn't hurt and doesn't suck," he added. "And I think it's kind of sad. It's actually, in some ways, saddest for the city of Edmonton, where we're from, because we were kind of this beacon of hope and excitement and possibility. We showed you could do something really special in a place that was not known for doing things like that."

Zeschuk and Muzyka retired from BioWare in 2012, the year Mass Effect 3 was released, so they've been away from the business for a considerable amount of time. They've moved on. "I've kind of gone through all the emotions long, long ago," Zeschuk explained.

articles.title: FromSoft's Switch 2 exclusive, The Duskbloods, has been delayed into 2027
articles.summary: FromSoftware's The Duskbloods - a game that is best described as Bloodborne meets Sekiro meets Dark Souls, with jetpacks and dinos thrown in - has been delayed from its 2026 launch window into an unspecified time in 2027.
body: "While development of The Duskbloods is at the final adjustment stage, we have made the decision to move the launch window to 2027," says a tweet from the game's official Twitter account. "We apologise to players who have been kindly awaiting the release of this title and thank you for your patience and support."

A follow-up message continued: "During the network test, we saw active interest in the core concepts of the game, including combat, strategic depth, and player expression. To further enhance these aspects, we have decided to move the launch, allowing time for final adjustments to game rules and balancing."

There was a suggestion previously that the title may have launched in September, but the prospective date for the unannounced release came and went without ceremony. Many consumers were uncertain whether the game would ever make its vague '2026' release window, given we've heard nothing from either publisher Nintendo or developer FromSoft since August's playtests.
points: FromSoftware's The Duskbloods - a game that is best described as Bloodborne meets Sekiro meets Dark Souls, with jetpacks and dinos thrown in - has been delayed from its 2026 launch window into an…

videos.summary: Don't miss the Launch Trailer for The Wolf Among Us Remastered, a remaster of the hit narrative-driven episodic adventure game developed by Telltale Games. Players will assume the role of the Big Bad Wolf as a murder in Fabletown leaves behind a conspiracy waiting to be solved.
body: #TheWolfAmongUsRemastered #Gaming #IGN
points: Don't miss the Launch Trailer for The Wolf Among Us Remastered, a remaster of the hit narrative-driven episodic adventure game developed by Telltale Games.
Players will assume the role of the Big Bad Wolf as a murder in Fabletown leaves behind a conspiracy waiting to be solved.
Explore new additions such as enhanced environments, upgraded lighting, remastered audio, and more.
The Wolf Among Us Remastered is available now for PlayStation 5 (PS5), Xbox One, and PC (Steam and Epic Games Store).

videos.title: Metro Redux - Next Gen Update Launch Trailer | PS5 Games
videos.summary: The METRO Redux Next Gen Update is live now, bringing a huge number of visual and performance upgrades to METRO 2033 & METRO Last Light! Plus it is FREE for all existing owners of METRO 2033 Redux and METRO Last Light Redux.
body: Console players can now experience true 4K at 60FPS or upscaled 4K at 120FPS, with native support for PlayStation® 5 and PlayStation® 5 Pro.
points: The METRO Redux Next Gen Update is live now, bringing a huge number of visual and performance upgrades to METRO 2033 & METRO Last Light!
